terms.grammar: question: the genitive of quality, “of how many years are you?”

terms.comment: Answered in the same form: Trēs annōs nātus sum, I’m three. The ordinal with agō counts the year one is in, which is one more: the same child quārtum annum agit, is in his fourth year, since the first year runs from birth to the first birthday (see age).

phrases.latin: Baba ferē nōnāgintā annōs nāta est, lenta quidem, sed suīs pedibus ambulat.
phrases.english: Baba is nearly ninety, slow indeed, but she walks on her own feet.

phrases.latin: quattuor et vīgintī fermē annōs nātus
Decem annōs est nātus. Ūndecimum agit (aetātis annum).
phrases.english: He’s ten: he is in his eleventh year.

sources: The phrase is composed; the grouped card gave no source.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Fōrm. VI 19 is from the Latīnitās loci collection of Franmōrārius, Dē variīs Latīnīs Graecīsque colloquendī fōrmulīs, a modern book; the classical instances are cited beside it.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 330.
